title: Selected generators form a basis after localization of a split module
statement: For a commutative ring A, a finitely generated module M generated by a finite family x, and a split injection of M into A^n, every prime p has a principal neighborhood where some subset of x is a basis of M.

source.place: Lemma Tag 07C6 proof, after the split conormal sequence

proof.text: For the globally split helper, finite generation and Module.Projective.of_split give finite presentation. Localize at the prime, use Module.exists_basis_of_span_of_flat to select a subfamily, enumerate its image by Fin c, and bound c by m using injectivity of the selection and by n using the localized split injection and finrank. Module.FinitePresentation.exists_notMem_bijective spreads the prescribed linear-combination isomorphism to a principal neighborhood.

Apply the globally split helper over B = A[1/b] to the images of x and the prime q = pB. The prime exists since b is outside p, and the localized family spans by span_eq_top_of_isLocalizedModule. This gives s outside q, a subset V, its enumeration e, and a prescribed basis over B[1/s].

Write s * image(b)^k = image(t) using IsLocalization.Away.surj. If t were in p then s would be in q, since image(b)^k is a unit. Thus t is outside p. The elements image(t) and s are associated in B, so IsLocalization.Away.mul_of_associated identifies B[1/s] as a localization of A away from b*t.

For the composite module map f followed by g, verify IsLocalizedModule.Away.mk at b*t. Multiplication by b*t is invertible over B[1/s]. For surjectivity, clear image(t)^i under g and b^j under f, then multiply the resulting lift by b^i*t^j to obtain denominator (b*t)^(i+j). For equality, clear image(t)^i under g and b^j under f and multiply the resulting equality by b^i*t^j.

Use IsLocalizedModule.linearEquiv for the composite and canonical localization maps; extend it to the localized coefficient ring, map the basis, and change coefficients along IsLocalization.algEquiv. IsLocalizedModule.linearEquiv_apply proves that each selected original generator maps to its canonical localization, while V, c, e and their bounds remain unchanged.

mathlib_searches.query: every generating family contains a basis over a local ring

lean.statement:
theorem exists_selected_basis_away_mul_of_split
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M]
    (n m : ℕ) (x : Fin m → M) (hx : Submodule.span A (Set.range x) = ⊤)
    (p : Ideal A) [p.IsPrime] (b : A) (hb : b ∉ p)
    (d : LocalizedModule.Away b M →ₗ[Localization.Away b] (Fin n → Localization.Away b))
    (l : (Fin n → Localization.Away b) →ₗ[Localization.Away b] LocalizedModule.Away b M)
    (hld : l.comp d = LinearMap.id) :
    ∃ t : A, t ∉ p ∧ ∃ (V : Finset (Fin m)) (c : ℕ),
      V.card = c ∧ c ≤ min n m ∧
      ∃ e : Fin c ≃ V,
        ∃ bs : Module.Basis (Fin c) (Localization.Away (b * t))
            (LocalizedModule.Away (b * t) M),
          ∀ j : Fin c, bs j =
            LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (Submonoid.powers (b * t)) M (x (e j).1)
